verdict: CoreWeave's revenue more than tripled to $1.21B and the core business made a small operating profit — but $267M of net interest costs on its datacenter debt turned that into a $291M net loss.

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out GPU-powered datacenter capacity to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; revenue more than tripled as new capacity came online.

opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $183M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up from $4M a year ago as the sales effort scaled.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration; up from $22M a year ago, including costs of becoming a public company.

follow100Note: Interest on the debt that funds CoreWeave's datacenters is the big leak: other expense — mostly $267M of net interest — took $21.60 of every $100 of revenue.
otherDetail: Other expense of $262M net was almost all interest: $267M of net interest expense on the borrowing that funds GPUs and datacenters, partly offset by $5M of other income. There was no fair-value adjustment gain or loss this quarter.
footerNote: CoreWeave reports one segment. Tax was a $48M charge even on a pre-tax loss, driven by its structure and foreign operations.

takeaways.title: Revenue more than tripled
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 207% to $1,213M as CoreWeave raced to add GPU capacity, ending the quarter with about 470 MW of active power. Revenue backlog reached $30.1B, including a $4B expansion deal with OpenAI on top of the earlier $11.9B agreement.

takeaways.title: Interest turned a profit into a loss
takeaways.text: The core business earned $19M of operating income, but $267M of net interest expense — the cost of borrowing to build datacenters — plus a $48M tax charge produced a $291M GAAP net loss. On the company's adjusted basis, operating income was $200M.

takeaways.title: The rental economics still show through
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $753M, a 62% margin — the cash earnings of the datacenters before interest, tax and the heavy upfront cost of the machines themselves, which is exactly the bill the interest line represents.
